name: Lisdexamfetamine
drug_class: Central nervous system stimulant; prodrug of dextroamphetamine
route_note: Oral capsules or chewable tablets once daily in the morning.

discovery.note: Dextroamphetamine was covalently linked to the amino acid L-lysine to create an inactive prodrug intended to give smooth, long-lasting release and reduce misuse by injection or snorting.

tagline: Lysine-linked amphetamine prodrug for ADHD and binge eating disorder
summary: Lisdexamfetamine is an inactive prodrug in which dextroamphetamine is bonded to L-lysine. After absorption, red blood cells cleave it to release dextroamphetamine gradually, giving a long, smooth effect. It is approved for ADHD and was the first drug approved for moderate-to-severe binge eating disorder.
mechanism: Lisdexamfetamine itself is pharmacologically inactive. Peptidases in red blood cells hydrolyse the amide bond to release L-lysine and dextroamphetamine, whose rate of formation limits the speed of onset.

The released dextroamphetamine increases synaptic dopamine and noradrenaline through transporter-mediated release, VMAT2 disruption and TAAR1 activation. Rate-limited conversion is thought to blunt euphoria and reduce misuse by non-oral routes, though it remains controlled.
uses: Moderate-to-severe binge eating disorder in adults (US)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Vyvanse is approved for ADHD in children in February 2007; Shire acquires New River for about $2.6 billion.

history.title: Adults
history.detail: Approval is extended to adults with ADHD.

history.title: Europe
history.detail: Lisdexamfetamine is authorised as Elvanse in the UK and other European countries via a decentralised procedure (2012–2013).

history.title: Binge eating disorder
history.detail: It becomes the first drug approved by the FDA for binge eating disorder.

history.title: Takeda
history.detail: Takeda acquires Shire, taking over Vyvanse.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic lisdexamfetamine launches in the US in August 2023.

pk.half_life: Prodrug under 1 hour; dextroamphetamine about 10–12 hours
pk.metabolism: Hydrolysis in red blood cells to dextroamphetamine and L-lysine
pk.excretion: Renal, mainly as amphetamine and metabolites

serious: Sudden death and serious cardiovascular events in people with heart disease
safety.boxed_warning: High potential for abuse and misuse, which can lead to substance use disorder, including addiction; misuse and abuse can result in overdose and death. Assess risk before prescribing and monitor throughout treatment.

facts: The prodrug design means taking it intravenously does not produce the rapid peak of dextroamphetamine.
